- Restored `thread.rs` from upstream main: the lead-in test failed at Z77.5 instead of Z80.5. Restored the fix: 4 passed.

No goldens changed. No UI, importer, or fixture files changed. The extra kernel STEP and import suites do not apply.

Required before merge:

1. `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs:248` and `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs:226`: supply the required heavy-lane results for this safety change. The PR body lists only the quick gate and clippy. `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run` selects the motion and app heavy lanes. I ran the plan only; those lanes remain unverified. Run the heavy gate on the final head and add its lane results to the PR body. Current upstream [AGENTS.md, lines 597–605](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/blob/ab9955105d00023351562f2a2865f6e7b6247673/AGENTS.md#L597-L605) requires this evidence before the PR becomes ready. A dry run is not a pass.

No code defect was found in the reviewed changes. No machine run or app-level Fanuc G76 post run was performed.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Addressed: The latest review's missing heavy-lane evidence is already in the PR body and the prior response.

The recorded gate passed 220 steps with 0 failures on head `5de53b78267abc3f10eaac8b749f9e7ff81975f9`.
The motion heavy lane passed 56 tests. Both known-failure checks for #1950 matched their expected failures.
The app heavy lane passed 42 tests. These are existing results, not a new run.

The requested merge with current `upstream/main` at `58cb641ca` stopped on a logic conflict.
The hunk is in `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs`, in `thread_planned_in`, near line 241.
The PR computes `s_top = f.station_of(p.top_z)` and uses it in `k_hi`.
Main computes `s_hi_pass = f.station_of(p.top_z).max(s_hi)` and uses it in `k_hi`.
Both sides changed the same pass-limit calculation.

I aborted the merge as instructed. No source, test, or branch head changed. No push occurred.
I did not run a new gate, clippy, or mutation check after this stop.
The head remains `5de53b78267abc3f10eaac8b749f9e7ff81975f9`.
Please re-review the existing evidence. The conflicting hunk requires a decision before a merge refresh.

Re-review of the same head. The earlier finding is met. The PR conflicts with main, so the verdict is `conflicts`.

This is a SAFETY-tier review. The change affects threading pass extent and the meridian rest/gouge scan.

## Earlier finding

1. Heavy-lane results: met. The PR body now records `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` on this head: 220 steps, 0 failed. The motion heavy lane passed 56 tests. The app heavy lane passed 42 tests. Both #1950 known-failure checks matched. I did not run the heavy lane again.

## Conflict with main

Main at `97a880c53` has merged #2892 (`cf336a225`, Fixes #2878). That PR made the same two fixes:

- `crates/motion/src/turning/revolve.rs`: main has the same removal of the `w0`/`w1` push. This hunk merges cleanly.
- `crates/motion/src/turning/thread.rs:245`: main uses `let s_hi_pass = f.station_of(p.top_z).max(s_hi);` for `k_hi`. The PR uses `let s_top = f.station_of(p.top_z);`. Both sides changed the same line, so `git merge` stops.

The two forms give the same value. `blade::setup` sets `s_hi = f.station_of(top_z).min(d_hi)` (`crates/motion/src/turning/blade.rs:146`). Thus `s_hi <= station_of(top_z)` always, and `.max(s_hi)` changes nothing.

Recommended resolution at refresh: take main's side of `thread.rs`. After that, the PR adds only the four pinning tests and the decision file. Also update `docs/decisions/2879-thread-free-air-start.md` item 2 to say that main's `s_hi_pass` form landed in #2892. This refresh has a hand edit, so it is DELTA work.

## Local results

Built in a local worktree. Trial merge: `upstream/main` `97a880c53` + this head, with the `thread.rs` conflict resolved to main's side. The result differs from main only in the test file and the decision file.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | Passed: 1 step (`turning_thread_end_face`), 0 failed |
| `turning_thread_end_face` | 4 passed |
| `turning_thread` | 18 passed |
| `turning_thread_cycle` | 4 passed |
| `turning_thread_dips` | 9 passed |
| `turning_thread_infeed` | 10 passed |
| `turning_blade` | 11 passed |
| `turning_form` | 5 passed |
| `cargo clippy -j 8 -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` | Passed |

Extra suites run: `turning_thread`, `turning_thread_cycle`, `turning_thread_dips`, `turning_thread_infeed`, `turning_blade`, `turning_form`. No `testdata/` file and no importer code changed, so the kernel STEP and `feature_edge_g1_join` suites do not apply.

## Mutations (against the resolved trial merge)

- Restored `revolve.rs` from the merge base `5fdbed9bd`: red. 3 of 4 tests failed with false rest of 5.0 mm and 4.0 mm. Restored: green.
- Changed only the `k_hi` line in `thread.rs` back to `s_hi`: red. `free_air_lead_in_starts_in_front_of_end_face_and_judges_clean` failed with "got 77.5". Restored: green. (A whole-file revert does not compile on main, because #2892 changed the `attach_cycle` signature.)

The pins thus also guard main's fix from #2892. That is the value of this PR after the refresh.

## Other checks

- Goldens moved: none.
- No UI change, so no screenshots are necessary.
- No process file, dependency, `build.rs`, `scripts/` or `.github` change.
- The test file has a provenance comment and a gate map.

No code defect found. No app-level Fanuc G76 post run and no machine run were done.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
